questions.q: When an obstacle blocks one side of the road, vehicles on that side must yield by stopping or slowing down for oncoming traffic.
The traffic sign in the figure prohibits trucks with a capacity of 2 tons or more and heavy special vehicles.
Overtaking requires changing lanes to pass a vehicle ahead, a complex action that drivers should avoid whenever possible.
Overtaking a vehicle that is passing a general sarguson moped is considered double overtaking.
questions.explanation: This is not classified as double overtaking in Japan.

questions.q: When turning right on a one-way street, a vehicle must first approach the right edge of the road and decelerate near the intersection's center, adhering to any arrow markings (except at roundabouts).
The three traffic signals in the figure provide identical instructions for vehicles approaching from either direction.
When overtaking a bicycle to turn left, a driver may sound the horn to warn the cyclist and proceed.
questions.explanation: Drivers must slow down or stop to allow the bicycle to pass first.

questions.q: A vehicle can pass a stopped streetcar if no passengers are boarding or alighting in the safety zone.
questions.explanation: Vehicles must reduce speed in a safety zone with a stopped streetcar, even without passengers.

questions.q: When a police officer at an intersection raises their arms vertically after extending them horizontally in an east-west direction, vehicles traveling east or west must stop at the designated spot.
At a pedestrian or bicycle crossing, vehicles must stop immediately before the thick white line, if present.
The traffic sign in the figure forbids vehicles from making right turns or proceeding straight through the intersection.
Vehicles must reduce speed on both steep uphill and downhill slopes.
questions.explanation: There is no mandatory speed reduction for steep uphill slopes.

questions.q: A vehicle experiences a wheelbase differential when making left or right turns.
On a road with two lanes per direction, ordinary vehicles must use the right-hand lane for travel.
questions.explanation: Vehicles must generally use the left-hand lane, except when overtaking or in specific circumstances.

questions.q: The traffic sign in the figure indicates a student pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of nearby schools, kindergartens, or nurseries.

questions.q: No signal is required when a driver reverses their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers must use reverse lights or hand signals when backing up.

questions.q: To overtake, a driver should first signal with the turn indicator and then check for safety behind.
questions.explanation: Safety behind must be checked before signaling to overtake.

questions.q: A single driver or pedestrian ignoring traffic rules can cause confusion and potential accidents.
When driving in rain or feeling fatigued, a driver should increase the following distance due to extended stopping distances.
General mopeds in Japan are restricted to a maximum speed of 30 km/h.
The traffic sign shown in the figure alerts drivers to an upcoming intersection.
Drivers must stop or reduce speed to ensure safe passage for people using wheelchairs, guide dogs, or white/yellow canes, indicating physical disabilities.
In the lanes depicted in the figure, vehicles in lane A may move to lane B, but vehicles in lane B cannot move to lane A.
On a lightly trafficked road, changing lanes only requires signaling without a safety check.
questions.explanation: A safety check is mandatory when changing lanes, regardless of traffic volume.

questions.q: Overtaking is not permitted at or within 30 meters before a pedestrian crossing.
Vehicles are allowed to cross sidewalks or bicycle paths to enter or exit roadside areas.
A flashing red traffic light mandates a stop at the designated line, with vehicles proceeding only after confirming safety.
At an intersection with the traffic signal shown in the figure, vehicles can freely choose to go straight, turn left, or turn right.
questions.explanation: Mopeds or light vehicles using the two-step right turn method are not allowed to make a right turn at this signal.

questions.q: In Japan, operating a vehicle while wearing sandals without heel straps or high-heeled shoes is not allowed.
A driver in Japan must carry a valid driver's license or an Individual Number Card with license details at all times while driving.
A standard Japanese driver's license allows the operation of both ordinary mopeds and small special vehicles.
Japanese traffic law requires that children under 6 years old be secured in an approved child restraint system when riding in a vehicle.
If there is enough space on the left side of a vehicle ahead, overtaking can be performed by passing on the left.
questions.explanation: Overtaking must generally be done on the right side of the vehicle being overtaken, as per Japanese traffic rules.

questions.q: If a pedestrian is crossing near an intersection without a crosswalk, a vehicle should use the horn to warn them and continue.
questions.explanation: Vehicles must slow down or stop to allow pedestrians to cross safely, without using the horn.

questions.q: When seeing the traffic sign shown in the figure, a driver is required to stop their vehicle completely, even if no vehicles or pedestrians are present on either side.
In Japan, it is illegal to operate a vehicle while holding and using a mobile phone for calls or texting.
The pavement marking shown in the figure designates a zone where entry is prohibited.
questions.explanation: This marking indicates a zone where stopping is prohibited.

questions.q: The default speed limit for passenger cars on Japanese expressways, unless otherwise indicated, is 100 km/h.
A yellow traffic light allows vehicles to proceed with caution while monitoring other traffic.
questions.explanation: Vehicles must stop at the stop line when the light is yellow, unless stopping safely is not feasible.

questions.q: After changing lanes, a driver should stop signaling about 3 seconds after completing the maneuver.
questions.explanation: Signaling must cease immediately after the lane change is complete.

questions.q: In Japan, drivers must ensure that all passengers, including those in the rear seats, wear seatbelts during vehicle operation.
Worn tires shorten braking distance due to a larger contact area with the road.
questions.explanation: Worn tires reduce traction, resulting in a longer braking distance.

questions.q: Following the arrow in the figure is the correct way to enter a gas station on the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Vehicles must first move toward the road's center before turning right.

questions.q: The traffic sign shown in the figure prohibits vehicles from making U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits vehicles from crossing the road.

questions.q: The traffic sign shown permits non-bus vehicles to use the lane when no buses are nearby or traffic is low, except for special light vehicles, mopeds, and light vehicles.
questions.explanation: Non-bus vehicles may use the bus lane only in unavoidable cases, such as road construction or left turns.

questions.q: The pavement marking shown in the figure marks the end of a 50 km/h speed limit zone.
In the situation shown in the figure, vehicle B may pass before vehicle A.
questions.explanation: Vehicle A has priority, so vehicle B must wait.

questions.q: The traffic sign in the figure bans all traffic from passing through the road.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits vehicle passage, but pedestrians and small remote-controlled vehicles are permitted.

questions.q: The traffic sign in the figure mandates that general mopeds use a two-step right turn method.
questions.explanation: This sign requires general mopeds to make a direct right turn, like automobiles.

questions.q: If a local bus at a stop signals to merge, other vehicles can pass by using the horn to alert it.
questions.explanation: Other vehicles must slow down to avoid obstructing the bus merging into traffic.
